headline: Expanding Kathleen Valley via staged bottleneck de-risking, capturing upside in a rising lithium market while retaining ability to stop if market turns
reasoning: Liontown's expansion of Kathleen Valley will not deliver all tonnes at once but instead unlocks capacity incrementally by addressing bottlenecks in the plant. Each bottleneck resolved brings in early cash, allowing the company to capitalise on a rising lithium price while de-risking the project. If the market deteriorates, works can be paused, having already captured some upside. Capital allocation priorities are: sustaining the business first, servicing debt second, then growth. A formal capital allocation framework is being developed to give the market more guidance. Ottaviano noted he and board/management are large personal shareholders, signalling long-term alignment and eventual dividend intention.
quote: We've been very public in the fact that our expansion will not deliver the tons all in one go, as a typical expansion would normally do. We're effectively expanding the plants. It's an exercise of bottleneck around our constraint. So as we do bottleneck a particular area of the plant that will unlock capacity and as that unlocks capacity, brings in early cash. So therefore we can capitalize on the rising market by unlocking those tons through this bottleneck that de-risk the project. And should the market turn, then we can stop but still have, um, taken advantage of that increasing price.
episode_title: Liontown sees a bigger lithium prize ahead

headline: Lithium spot price up 250%; recovery seen as sustainable driven by low spodumene/lithium carbonate inventories in China, strong EV demand and slower new supply coming to market
reasoning: Lithium carbonate inventory levels in China are at their lowest since 2024, tightening the supply of feedstock for LFP batteries, the dominant EV battery chemistry. Demand from the world's largest EV market is strong and growing. On the supply side, capital costs are rising, approval timelines are lengthening and productivity is falling, meaning new projects will take longer to reach production. Brownfields expansions are the fastest route to new supply, which structurally favours existing producers. Ottaviano also argues lithium is still an early-stage maturing commodity going through growing pains similar to other commodities decades ago, and that as pricing mechanisms become more transparent, volatility will reduce and investment confidence will improve.
quote: If we look at the fundamentals which are driving the improvement, they are strong inventory levels in the biggest market being China, are at levels that we haven't seen since 2024. And these are inventory levels of calcium lithium carbonate, which is the main feedstock in LFP batteries which are the most commonly used battery in EVs. So therefore if we look at the fundamentals, the demand is strong. Inventory levels are low, which means the suppliers are short of product. The other point to add here is supply from producers will take longer to bring on into the market. As the market is assuming it's only getting tougher. Capital costs are increasing, approval times are getting longer. Productivity is getting lower, so new projects will take longer to come on. And the quickest way to production are brownfields expansions. And that's exactly what we're doing at Kathleen Valley.
episode_title: Liontown sees a bigger lithium prize ahead
